benchmarks.description: Abstraction and reasoning tasks built to resist contamination and memorization, scored independently by ARC Prize. Successor to ARC-AGI-1, which frontier models have saturated.

Agentic automation of realistic business workflows across six domains, run against 47 simulated SaaS tools. Scored strict pass/fail per task. Zapier runs the official leaderboard on a held-out private set, so its numbers and a vendor's own run are separate measurements.

Original long-horizon software-engineering tasks in live repositories; 113 tasks across five languages, graded by program verifiers on the agent's committed code. v1.1 regrades in a clean isolated environment and is not comparable with v1.
Graduate-level Google-proof Q&A, Diamond subset (the harder questions).
Expert-level questions across many domains; closed-book reasoning.
pass@1 for hand-written code completion problems. Older but still widely cited.

Long-horizon computer-use workflows across real desktop applications; 108 tasks, a median one taking a human about 1.6 hours. Scored as the partial-credit rate; the authors' primary metric is the stricter all-or-nothing completion rate, which is not recorded.
Resolution rate on real-world GitHub issues, Pro variant (successor to Verified).
Long-horizon terminal command tasks, Terminal-Bench 2.x. Pools 2.0 and 2.1, which share a scale. Superseded by 3.0 and 4.0, whose scores are not comparable.
Long-horizon general agent tasks (Terminal-Bench 3.0); much harder than 2.x, scores are not comparable across versions.
Long-horizon general agent tasks (Terminal-Bench 4.0). A breaking update over 3.0 - saturated tasks removed, 19 tasks fixed, a flat 8h agent timeout - so scores are not comparable across versions.
Agentic scientific-research tasks in a terminal, version 0.1. A separate line from the numbered Terminal-Bench versions; scores are not comparable with them.
